similarities.point: Both describe Thrace as a region in Southeast Europe.
similarities.quote_britannica: THIROCE, the ancient stone of a country in the S.E. of Europe, now forming part of European Turkey.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: Thrace (/ θ r eɪ s /, thrayss) is a geographical and historical region in Southeast Europe roughly corresponding to the province of Thrace in the Roman Empire.

similarities.point: Both state that the name was once applied to a wider area including Macedonia and Scythia.
similarities.quote_britannica: In the earliest times the name was sent in a vastay seen, and applied to the whole region such of the Afghan Sen, including Macedonia and even Seythisu but with this morning become better known to the Greeky.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: The ancient Greeks employed the term "Thrace" to refer to all of the territory which lay north of Thessaly inhabited by the Thracians, a region which "had no definite boundaries" and to which other regions (like Macedonia and even Scythia) were added.

similarities.point: Both state that the term was later confined to narrower and more definite limits.
similarities.quote_britannica: Three was confined within narrower and more definite limits.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: As the Greeks gained knowledge of world geography, "Thrace" came to designate the area bordered by the Danube on the north, by the Euxine Sea (Black Sea) on the east, by northern Macedonia in the south, and by Illyria to the west.

similarities.point: Both mention that the region was bounded by the Danube to the north.
similarities.quote_britannica: It was bounded on the 7b, by the Danube, E. by the Exiton and the Boskolome, S. by the Proponents and the Aegean, and W. by the Strymon, or, as a later period by the Neustus, and the separated in from Macedonia.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: As the Greeks gained knowledge of world geography, "Thrace" came to designate the area bordered by the Danube on the north, by the Euxine Sea (Black Sea) on the east, by northern Macedonia in the south, and by Illyria to the west.

differences.point: Britannica says the region now forms part of European Turkey, while Wikipedia says it comprises parts of Bulgaria, Greece, and Turkey.
differences.quote_britannica: THIROCE, the ancient stone of a country in the S.E. of Europe, now forming part of European Turkey.
differences.quote_wikipedia: it comprises present-day southeastern Bulgaria (Northern Thrace), northeastern Greece (Western Thrace), and the European part of Turkey (East Thrace).

differences.point: Britannica gives the southern boundary as the Propontis and the Aegean, while Wikipedia gives northern Macedonia as the southern limit.
differences.quote_britannica: It was bounded on the 7b, by the Danube, E. by the Exiton and the Boskolome, S. by the Proponents and the Aegean, and W. by the Strymon, or, as a later period by the Neustus, and the separated in from Macedonia.
differences.quote_wikipedia: As the Greeks gained knowledge of world geography, "Thrace" came to designate the area bordered by the Danube on the north, by the Euxine Sea (Black Sea) on the east, by northern Macedonia in the south, and by Illyria to the west.

differences.point: Britannica says the northern boundary was later reduced to the chain of the same (Haemus), while Wikipedia says the Byzantine theme contained only East Thrace.
differences.quote_britannica: After the Roman conquest, its size was still further reduced by the chain of the same being made its northern boundary.
differences.quote_wikipedia: The medieval Byzantine theme of Thrace contained only what today is East Thrace.

differences.point: Britannica equates the region with modern Rumelia including Macedonia and Thessaly, while Wikipedia says Rumeli is the Turkish name for Thrace.
differences.quote_britannica: It corresponds parting with the modern Rumell, which also includes part of Macedonia and Thessaly.
differences.quote_wikipedia: In Turkish, Thrace is commonly referred to as Rumeli, meaning "Land of the Romans", which was the name traditionally given by Turkic societies to the Byzantine Empire and Orthodox Christians.

wiki_only_topics.topic: Etymology and Greek mythology of the name Thrace
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: The word Thrace, from ancient Greek Thrake (Θρᾴκη), referred originally to the Thracians (ancient Greek Thrâikes Θρᾷκες), an ancient people inhabiting Southeast Europe.

wiki_only_topics.topic: Ancient names Aria and Perke according to Stephanus of Byzantium
wiki_only_topics.quote_wikipedia: Sixth century geographer Stephanus of Byzantium claimed that, long before the ancient Greeks started referring to the region as Thrace, it was known as Aria (Aría Ἀρία) and Perke (Pérkē Πέρκη).
The largest cities of Thrace are: Istanbul, Plovdiv, Çorlu, Tekirdağ, Burgas, Edirne, Stara Zagora, Sliven, Yambol, Haskovo, Komotini, Alexandroupoli, Xanthi, and Kırklareli.
Most of the Bulgarian and Greek population are Orthodox Christians, while most of the Turkish inhabitants of Thrace are Sunni Muslims.
The Thracians appear in Homer 's Iliad as Trojan allies, led by Acamas and Peiros.
